vision: A compassionate and inclusive society where every person can live with dignity, hope, and equal opportunity, regardless of economic condition, health status, identity, or background.
mission: To empower children, people living with HIV, and underserved communities by improving access to education, health support, essential resources, and sustainable opportunities.
intro: Naya Aasha(New Hope) is a non governmental organization based in Lalitpur, Nepal, working with children whose schooling is interrupted by cost, people living with HIV, and low income families in need of practical support. Our programs cover children's education, HIV care and inclusion, family and emergency assistance, and community health awareness. Naya Aasha is registered under the Organization Registration Act 2034 of Nepal with the District Administration Office, Lalitpur (Regd. No. 4447/073 ), 2016, October 18 and is affiliated with the Social Welfare Council under section 13 of the Social Welfare Act, 1992 (SWC).
story: Naya Aasha was created from a simple belief: difficult circumstances should never decide the limits of a person’s future. We bring people, skills, and resources together to help communities address urgent needs while building pathways toward long-term independence.
founderMessage:
When Naya Aasha began, we had no office, no funding, and no certainty that it would work. What we had was a conviction that difficult circumstances should never decide the limits of a person's future and a refusal to accept how ordinary it had become for families to be told that nothing could be done.

We work with children whose education is interrupted by cost, with people living with HIV who face stigma more often than they face a shortage of medicine, and with families managing more than any family should have to manage alone. We do not pretend these problems are simple, and we do not pretend we can solve them by ourselves.

What we can promise is this. We listen before we act. We do not make commitments we cannot keep. We protect the privacy and dignity of every person who comes to us, especially those who are most easily overlooked. And we account openly for what we receive and what we spend, because trust given to an organization like ours is not owed  it is earned, and it can be lost.

Naya Aasha is not the work of one person. It belongs to the volunteers who give their time, the partners who share their expertise, the supporters who make our programmes possible, and above all the families who allow us into some of the hardest moments of their lives. That last trust is the one we take most seriously.

There is a great deal still to build. If our work speaks to you, we would welcome you in it.
title: A new hope, built together.
